The first-order logic formula can be written as:

\[
\forall x \, (Cloud(x) \land ReleasesWaterDroplets(x) \rightarrow \exists y \, Occurs(Rain(y)))

- Let \( \text{CostumeDesigner}(x) \) be a predicate that is true if \( x \) is a skilled costume designer.
- Let \( \text{twinkle} \) be a constant representing Twinkle.

The sentence "If Twinkle has mastery over magic, then she is either an excellent seamstress or a skilled costume designer, but not both" can be translated as:

\text{Mastery}(\text{twinkle}) \rightarrow \left( (\text{Seamstress}(\text{twinkle}) \oplus \text{CostumeDesigner}(\text{twinkle})) \right)
\]
